deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is Dedekind's draft of a section 'Intervalle'. It generalises the two classes of a cut of the rationals Q (=R in his notation). The previous page defined an interval as a set A ⊆ Q such that x ∈ A whenever a1 < x < a2 with a1, a2 ∈ A (order-convexity). It also characterised a first class A1 as a downward-closed proper subset. The page opens by finishing that characterisation of the second class: if a2 ∈ A2, then every larger rational also lies in A2, so A2 is upward closed.

Left column, step by step:
(1) Definition 'Stück'. A is a Stück (piece) of B iff every element of A is in B, i.e. A ⊆ B. The right column notes that every interval is a Stück of R=Q.
(2) Definition 'benachbart' (adjacent). Intervals A, B are adjacent iff A ∩ B = ∅ and A ∪ B =: C is again an interval.
(3) Claim: the two classes A1, A2 of a cut are adjacent. Proof (filled in by me, routine): A1 ∩ A2 = ∅ by definition of a cut, and A1 ∪ A2 = Q, which is an interval.
(4) Planned enumeration of all possible relations between two intervals A, B. Only case 1) 'no common number' is written; case 2) and the rest are left blank (dots).
(5) Complements. To each interval A belong two further sets A', A'' that complete A to Q:
 - A' = {x ∈ Q : x < a for every a ∈ A};
 - A'' = {x ∈ Q : x > a for every a ∈ A}.
 Proof that A', A, A'' partition Q (mine): if x ∉ A and x is neither below all of A nor above all of A, then there are a1 < x < a2 with a1, a2 ∈ A. Convexity then gives x ∈ A, a contradiction. Disjointness is clear. A' and A'' are themselves intervals (downward resp. upward closed), possibly empty.
(6) Method for classifying relations. The relation between A and B is determined by which of the nine intersections X ∩ Y are nonempty, where X ∈ {A', A, A''} and Y ∈ {B', B, B''}. That is, a 3×3 intersection pattern serves as the invariant classifying the mutual position of two intervals.

Right column:
(7) The union of two adjacent intervals is written as a product: C = AB if every a < every b, and C = BA if every a > every b. Implicit lemma (mine): for disjoint nonempty intervals, one of these two alternatives always holds. Proof: suppose a1 < b1 and b2 < a2 with ai ∈ A, bi ∈ B. Since b1 ≠ a2, either b1 < a2, which puts b1 in A, or b1 > a2, which puts a2 in B; both are contradictions. Hence the notation AB/BA is well defined and order-sensitive (non-commutative juxtaposition).

The next page goes on to 'addition of intervals' (Minkowski sums A+B), proving that A+B is again an interval.
errors: No outright errors. Empty interval: if A = ∅, the definitions give A' = A'' = Q, so A', A, A'' no longer partition Q. Dedekind tacitly assumes A nonempty (the same tacit assumption is needed for the AB/BA dichotomy).
The enumeration of the cases of relations between two intervals is left incomplete (only case 1 is stated).
The right-column remark C = AB or BA presupposes the unstated lemma that two disjoint intervals lie entirely on one side of each other. The lemma is true, but it is not proved on the page.

results.what: Definition of intervals of rationals as order-convex sets, with cut classes as special cases; subset ('Stück') and adjacency ('benachbart') of intervals
results.modern_name: convex subsets of a linear order; adjacent convex sets
results.usually_credited_to: folklore; order-convexity is standard in order theory (Hausdorff 1914 and others)

results.what: Classes of a Dedekind cut are adjacent intervals whose union is Q
results.modern_name: Dedekind cut as a partition of Q into an initial and a final segment

results.what: Every nonempty interval A induces the partition Q = A' ∪ A ∪ A'' (lower part, A, upper part)
results.modern_name: decomposition of a linear order relative to a convex set (initial segment / convex set / final segment)

results.what: Classifying the mutual position of two intervals by the 3×3 pattern of nonempty intersections between {A', A, A''} and {B', B, B''}
results.modern_name: analogue of the 9-intersection model / Allen's interval algebra (qualitative interval relations)
results.usually_credited_to: J. F. Allen 1983 (13 interval relations); Egenhofer & Franzosa 1991 (9-intersection model, in a topological setting)

results.what: Disjoint intervals are linearly ordered (all a < all b or all a > all b); ordered juxtaposition AB for the union of adjacent intervals
results.modern_name: ordered sum / concatenation of convex pieces of a linear order
results.usually_credited_to: folklore; ordered sums of order types go back to Cantor 1895

deep.surprise_reason: The definitions are elementary order-theoretic preparations for a reworked theory of cuts. The idea of classifying all relations between two intervals by the 3×3 intersection pattern of (lower complement, interval, upper complement) is a neat structural device. It resembles the much later 9-intersection model and Allen-style interval algebra. However, the enumeration is left unfinished, and the idea is mathematically simple, so this is a curiosity rather than a significant anticipation.

checkable.asserts: Two cut classes (−∞,0] and (0,∞) are disjoint with union the whole line, i.e. adjacent (model over the reals).
The two classes of a cut have no common element.
(0,1) and (1,2) are disjoint, but their union omits 1 and is not an interval, so they are not adjacent.
For A=[1,3], A'=(−∞,1) and A''=(3,∞) together with A cover the line (the A', A, A'' partition).

checkable.sympy: Interval.open(-oo, 1).intersect(Interval(1, 3)) == S.EmptySet and Interval(1, 3).intersect(Interval.Lopen(3, oo)) == S.EmptySet
checkable.asserts: A', A, A'' are pairwise disjoint in the example.

transcription_corrections: Line 'welche ein{+es+} jedes der drei Intervalle': the manuscript reads 'welche ein jedes der drei Intervalle A', A, A'' gemeinschaftlich hat mit jedem der drei Intervalle B', B, B''' (the comma before 'mit' is incidental). The meaning is the pairwise intersections.
Right column: the struck-out word before 'a > b' is illegible (looks like 'bzw' or a false start). The intended text is 'je nachdem die Zahlen a < b oder a > b sind'.
The inserted 'A' after 'Zu jedem Intervall' and the inserted 'a′' after 'alle Zahlen' are interlinear additions, correctly marked.
